title: Voice In, Visuals Out: The Agony and the Ecstasy - Allen Pike, Forestwalk Labs
talk_summary: Allen Pike describes building voice-in/visuals-out AI experiences at Forestwalk Labs, where a voice agent joins calls and files issues in real time. He argues the key engineering constraints are latency (sub-second response), fast small models, eager short-interval inference, and aggressive prefix caching.

takeaways.what_they_do: They structure requests so the first ~90% of the context window is identical across calls, leaving only the final ~10% variable, to exploit provider prefix caching.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to the first 90% of the context window if we can to be the same from request to request, and then just use that final 10%

takeaways.technique: Fast model for interactive turns, big model async for heavy work
takeaways.what_they_do: A small fast model handles real-time responses and hands off larger chunks of work asynchronously to a bigger model, then re-interleaves results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that model then hands off or sends off an asynchronous message to a larger model that can think

takeaways.technique: Latency-prioritized inference platform, not just small model
takeaways.what_they_do: They found a cheaper small model (GPT-5 mini) had terrible P95 latency, while a Haiku-class model on a latency-prioritizing platform was consistently fast.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we were seeing latencies of 5,000 milliseconds, 7,000 P95, sometimes 10,000 millisecond latency for this small model
takeaways.numbers: 5,000-10,000ms P95 for GPT-5 mini vs Haiku much better

takeaways.technique: Eager short-interval inference instead of waiting for completion
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than waiting for a full turn/silence, they fire inference every 1-2 seconds as input arrives so partial work is done incrementally.
takeaways.evidence_quote: being willing to send inference every 1 or 2 seconds as they speak

takeaways.technique: Minimize output tokens for fast cheap turns
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly cap output token count to keep inference turns fast and affordable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: minimize the number of output tokens so that you can get these really fast and relatively affordable inference turns
